newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds see Mexico in stg, await Czech Export.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds see Mexico in stg, await Czech Export.

text.p: The primary market saw Mexico launch a 300 million stg five-year bond on Wednesday to yield 175 basis points over gilts.
Joint lead managers for the transaction were BZW and SBC Warburg.
Mexico last went to the sterling market in November 1991, placing a 100 million sterling bond, coming due in December 1998. In 1981, it had placed a 50 million sterling issue due in September 2008.
The Mexican government has been able to cover its maturing market debt issues for 1997, which were only about $1.4 billion, by going to capital markets early at the start of the year.
But it has also been paying back what it owes to the International Monetary Fund. It most recently made a $590 million payment in February.
"Mexico has gone well, Mexico is not going to be a blow-out on the first day but it is the largest emerging market deal that's been done in sterling," a syndicate official said.
"30 percent of our book went to the UK," he added.
SBC Warburg said Turkey was increased due to demand for the deal predominantly out of Switzerland but also from Germany and Britain.
"We continue to see demand and the spread has tightened to around 340 bid from the 350 launch spread," a syndicate official said.

Meanwhile Credit Suisse First Boston arranged a high-yielding sterling bond as part of financing for the purchase of the BBC's domestic radio and television transmission network, the bank said on Wednesday.
A 125 million stg 10-year bond was launched in the name of Castle Transmission Services, an international consortium, at a spread of 195 basis points over gilts.

Dealers said effective pre-marketing meant the deal was quickly sold out and the spread tightened to 185 b.p. bid. Distribution of sales was predominantly to British institutional investors and the rest to investors in continental Europe.
